summary: Match the fluid to the patient AND the setting. Balanced crystalloid is a sepsis-shaped default that does NOT transfer to TBI (saline wins there). D5W and half-normal are not resuscitation fluids. HES is avoided. Permissive hypotension outside TBI until hemorrhage is controlled.

body.text: *Albumin electrolyte content varies by manufacturer/carrier — check the product label. Normal saline is not 'normal': its chloride (154) sits far above plasma (~100–106); large-volume harm is dose-dependent, from the chloride load causing a non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis. LR's potassium is NOT a reason to withhold it in hyperkalemia. Plasma-Lyte is calcium-free (runs with blood) and buffers via acetate metabolized in muscle, so it needs no liver.

body.text: 2020 sequential network meta-analysis: the 'best' fluid reverses by population. In SEPSIS, balanced crystalloids reduced mortality more than saline (OR 0.84) and HES (OR 0.81). In TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY that flips — saline and starch achieved lower mortality than albumin and balanced crystalloids, saline significantly outperforming albumin (OR 0.55). 'Always use balanced crystalloid' is a sepsis-shaped default; in TBI, saline's higher effective tonicity matters more than a balanced solution's acid-base profile.

Bickell 1994 (n=598, penetrating torso trauma, prehospital SBP ≤ 90): delayed resuscitation (fluid withheld until operative control) had higher survival to discharge (70% vs 62%, p=0.04). Theory: aggressive crystalloid before hemorrhage control 'pops the clot' and drives dilutional coagulopathy, anemia, and hypothermia. Founding-trial limits: single-center, penetrating torso only, crystalloid (pre-dates blood-ratio evidence), and BP was actually similar between groups. Current practice: target SBP ~80–90 or MAP ~50 in pure hemorrhagic shock (EAST) until hemorrhage is controlled — with a carve-out for concurrent TBI, where a higher SBP target is needed.

PROPPR (JAMA 2015): 1:1:1 vs 1:1:2 plasma:platelets:RBC — NO significant difference in 24-h or 30-day mortality, though more 1:1:1 patients achieved hemostasis and fewer died of exsanguination in the first 24 h. Balanced-ratio transfusion is widely adopted despite the negative primary endpoint, built substantially on observational data with real survivorship bias (you have to survive long enough to receive the later components). An earlier RCT (Nascimento 2013) trended toward HIGHER mortality with the balanced ratio.
Prehospital plasma — a genuinely contradictory record

body.text: RePHILL is the trial that actually tested LYOPHILIZED plasma prehospital and was negative on both primary outcomes. A post hoc PAMPer+COMBAT pooling found the benefit concentrated in transport times > 20 min — the effect, where real, may be time/distance-dependent rather than universal. TCCC 21-01 (2021) designates cold-stored low-titer group O whole blood as the preferred resuscitation fluid for hemorrhagic shock and removed crystalloids from the recommended options; freeze-dried plasma is the room-temperature-stable fallback where the cold chain can't be maintained.

Ezplaz (Vascular Solutions / Teleflex) — the first FDA-licensed freeze-dried plasma in the US (July 29 2026). Room-temperature stable, no thaw, reconstitutes in ~1 min with the included sterile water, plastic packaging. Supplied as group AB and group A low-titer anti-B (selected to be safe across likely recipient types before the recipient's blood type is known — not 'give without regard to ABO'). Licensed for adults needing plasma when other plasma products are not available: active bleeding, massive transfusion, some bleeding patients on warfarin.

items: Starch (HES): avoid — kidney injury and mortality signal confirmed in CHEST and 6S.
D5W for 'dehydration': drops sodium — mostly free water once metabolized, the wrong fix for volume depletion.
Balanced fluid in head injury: use saline instead — the mild hypotonicity of LR / Plasma-Lyte can worsen cerebral edema.
Hypotonic fluid to resuscitate: won't fill the tank — distributes out of the vascular space too quickly.

Warm the fluid: TCCC targets 38 °C, ATLS 39 °C. A single 2 L room-temperature bolus drops core temp only ~0.3 °C — active warming is about the cumulative multi-liter scenario and cold-ambient-equilibrated bags.
